senses.en: a long, harsh period of questioning or investigation
(the Inquisition) a Catholic court that punished heresy in past centuries

ex.en: The job interview felt more like an inquisition than a conversation.
ex.zh: 那場求職面試感覺比較像審訊，而不是對談。

senses.en: curious and eager to learn
too interested in other people's affairs

ex.en: The inquisitive child asked dozens of questions about the stars.
ex.zh: 那個好奇的孩子問了好幾十個關於星星的問題。

root.note: 喜歡深入追問的 → 好奇的

senses.en: a person who questions others harshly
an official of the Inquisition

ex.en: The reporter questioned the mayor like a stern inquisitor.
ex.zh: 記者像嚴厲的審問者一樣質問市長。

root.note: 深入追問的人 → 審問者

senses.en: (usually plural) progress made in entering a new area or market
a sudden attack into enemy territory

ex.en: The new phone brand made its first inroad into the Asian market.
ex.zh: 這個新手機品牌首次打入亞洲市場。

root.note: 騎馬闖入 → 侵入；打入

mn: 常見片語 make inroads into：打入、侵蝕。

senses.en: impossible to satisfy
senses.zh: 無法滿足的；貪得無厭的

ex.en: She has an insatiable appetite for mystery novels.
ex.zh: 她對推理小說的胃口永遠填不飽。

senses.en: to write or carve words on a surface
to write a dedication in a book

ex.en: The jeweler will inscribe their initials inside the ring.
ex.zh: 珠寶師會把他們名字的縮寫刻在戒指內側。

senses.en: impossible to understand or interpret
senses.zh: 難以捉摸的；高深莫測的

ex.en: The poker player kept an inscrutable expression throughout the game.
ex.zh: 那位撲克玩家整場都保持著讓人看不透的表情。

root.note: 無法看透的 → 難以捉摸的

senses.en: lacking confidence; anxious
senses.zh: 沒有安全感的；缺乏自信的

senses.en: not safe or firmly fixed

ex.en: Many teenagers feel insecure about their appearance.
ex.zh: 許多青少年對自己的外表缺乏自信。

root.note: 不能免於憂慮的 → 沒有安全感的

senses.en: unconscious
unaware of or indifferent to something
too small to be noticed

ex.en: He seemed insensible to the danger he was in.
ex.zh: 他似乎沒意識到自己身處危險之中。

mn: insensible 不是 sensible（明智的）的反義，而是「沒感覺」。

senses.en: lacking the ability to feel or perceive

ex.en: A rock is an insentient object that feels neither heat nor pain.
ex.zh: 石頭是無知覺的物體，既感覺不到熱也感覺不到痛。

senses.en: unable to be separated; always together

ex.en: The two cousins were inseparable as children.
ex.zh: 這兩個表兄弟小時候形影不離。

senses.en: spreading gradually and quietly in a harmful way

ex.en: High blood pressure is an insidious disease with few early symptoms.
ex.zh: 高血壓是一種悄悄危害健康的疾病，早期幾乎沒有症狀。

root.note: 坐在裡面埋伏的 → 暗中為害的

senses.en: a deep and accurate understanding of someone or something

ex.en: The documentary offers insight into the lives of deep-sea fishermen.
ex.zh: 這部紀錄片讓人深入了解深海漁民的生活。

senses.en: the quality of being too small or unimportant to matter

ex.en: Looking at the night sky made him feel his own insignificance.
ex.zh: 仰望夜空讓他感受到自己的渺小。

root.note: 沒有意義 → 微不足道

senses.en: too small or unimportant to be worth considering

ex.en: The difference in price between the two stores was insignificant.
ex.zh: 兩家店的價差微不足道。

root.note: 不具意義的 → 不重要的

senses.en: to suggest something bad in an indirect way
to gradually work oneself into a position

ex.en: Are you trying to insinuate that I cheated on the test?
ex.zh: 你是在暗示我考試作弊嗎？

root.note: 彎彎曲曲地鑽進去 → 拐彎抹角地暗示

senses.en: lacking flavor
dull and uninteresting

ex.en: Critics called the movie's plot predictable and insipid.
ex.zh: 影評說這部電影情節老套又乏味。

root.note: 沒有味道的 → 乏味的

senses.en: the act of firmly demanding something or refusing to accept refusal

ex.en: At my mother's insistence, I wore a heavy coat.
ex.zh: 在我媽的堅持下，我穿了厚外套。

root.note: 站在原地不動 → 堅持

senses.en: demanding something firmly and not accepting refusal
continuing in a way that is hard to ignore

ex.en: She was insistent that we stay for dinner.
ex.zh: 她堅持要我們留下來吃晚飯。

root.note: 站著不動的 → 堅持的

senses.en: rude and disrespectful behavior

ex.en: The soldier was punished for his insolence toward the officer.
ex.zh: 那名士兵因對軍官無禮而受罰。

root.note: 不合慣例的態度 → 無禮

senses.en: rude and showing no respect

ex.en: The insolent customer shouted at the waiter over a small mistake.
ex.zh: 那個無禮的客人為了一點小錯就對服務生大吼。

root.note: 不合慣例的 → 無禮的

senses.en: the inability to sleep well

ex.en: Drinking coffee late at night can cause insomnia.
ex.zh: 深夜喝咖啡可能導致失眠。

root.note: 無法睡眠的症狀 → 失眠

senses.en: an official whose job is to check that rules are followed
a police officer of fairly high rank

ex.en: A health inspector visits the restaurant twice a year.
ex.zh: 衛生稽查員每年到這家餐廳檢查兩次。

root.note: 往裡面看的人 → 檢查員

senses.en: an example or single occurrence of something

ex.en: This is just one instance of how the program has helped students.
ex.zh: 這只是這個計畫如何幫助學生的其中一個例子。

root.note: 站在眼前的事 → 實例

mn: 常見片語 for instance：例如。

senses.en: happening immediately
a very short moment
(of food) prepared quickly and easily

ex.en: The new app was an instant success.
ex.zh: 這款新應用程式一推出就大受歡迎。

root.note: 就站在眼前的 → 立即的

senses.en: happening immediately, without delay

ex.en: The effect of the medicine was almost instantaneous.
ex.zh: 這種藥的效果幾乎是立即見效。

senses.en: to cause something to start, especially something bad

ex.en: The police believe a small group tried to instigate the riot.
ex.zh: 警方認為有一小群人試圖煽動這場暴動。

root.note: 用棒子戳使行動 → 煽動

senses.en: a person who causes something to start, especially trouble

ex.en: The teacher tried to find out who was the instigator of the food fight.
ex.zh: 老師想找出誰是這場食物大戰的始作俑者。

senses.en: to gradually establish an idea or feeling in someone's mind

ex.en: Good teachers instill a love of learning in their students.
ex.zh: 好老師會在學生心中培養對學習的熱愛。

root.note: 一滴一滴地滴進去 → 逐漸灌輸

senses.en: useful and informative; teaching something
senses.zh: 有教育意義的；有啟發性的

ex.en: It is instructive to compare how different countries handled the crisis.
ex.zh: 比較各國如何處理這場危機，很有啟發性。

root.note: 在心中建構知識的 → 有教育意義的

senses.en: the condition of not being enough
(medicine) the failure of an organ to work properly

ex.en: The project stalled because of an insufficiency of funds.
ex.zh: 這個計畫因為資金不足而停擺。

senses.en: not enough

ex.en: The judge ruled that there was insufficient evidence to convict him.
ex.zh: 法官裁定證據不足以定他的罪。

senses.en: narrow-minded and uninterested in outside ideas
relating to an island

ex.en: The small, insular community was suspicious of newcomers.
ex.zh: 這個封閉的小社區對新來的人抱持懷疑。

root.note: 像孤島一樣的 → 閉塞的

senses.en: to cover something to prevent heat, sound, or electricity from passing
to protect someone from unpleasant influences

ex.en: We need to insulate the attic before winter.
ex.zh: 我們得在冬天前幫閣樓做隔熱。

root.note: 使像孤島一樣隔開 → 隔絕

senses.en: impossible to overcome

ex.en: The team faced what seemed like insuperable obstacles.
ex.zh: 這支隊伍面臨看似無法克服的障礙。

root.note: 無法越過的 → 無法克服的

senses.en: impossible to hold back or control

ex.en: An insuppressible giggle escaped her during the serious speech.
ex.zh: 在嚴肅的演講中，她忍不住咯咯笑了出來。

senses.en: an uprising or rebellion against authority

ex.en: The government sent troops to put down the insurgence in the north.
ex.zh: 政府派軍隊鎮壓北方的叛亂。

senses.en: a person fighting against a government or authority
rising up against authority

ex.en: An insurgent group took control of the border town.
ex.zh: 一個叛亂團體控制了這座邊境城鎮。

senses.en: a violent uprising against a government

ex.en: The insurrection was crushed within a week.
ex.zh: 這場暴動在一週內就被鎮壓了。

senses.en: not able to be touched; not physical
hard to describe or define
senses.zh: 難以捉摸的；難以言說的

ex.en: Team spirit is an intangible quality that can win championships.
ex.zh: 團隊精神是一種能贏得冠軍的無形特質。

senses.en: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
the state of being whole and undivided

ex.en: She is a journalist of great integrity who never accepts bribes.
ex.zh: 她是一位非常正直的記者，從不收受賄賂。

root.note: 未被碰觸、完好無缺 → 完整；正直

senses.en: the ability to think logically and understand ideas
a very intelligent person

ex.en: She was admired for her sharp intellect and quick wit.
ex.zh: 她以敏銳的智力和機智受人欽佩。

root.note: 在事物之間做選擇的能力 → 智力

senses.en: relating to the ability to think and understand
a person who is highly educated and enjoys thinking about ideas

ex.en: Chess is a game that requires great intellectual effort.
ex.zh: 西洋棋是一種需要大量腦力的遊戲。

senses.en: the ability to learn, understand, and think
secret information gathered about an enemy or rival

ex.en: Crows show remarkable intelligence when solving puzzles.
ex.zh: 烏鴉在解謎時展現出驚人的智力。

root.note: 能在事物之間辨別的能力 → 智力

senses.en: able to be understood

ex.en: The static made his voice barely intelligible over the radio.
ex.zh: 雜訊讓他在無線電裡的聲音幾乎聽不清楚。

senses.en: lack of self-control, especially in drinking alcohol

ex.en: His intemperance eventually ruined both his health and his career.
ex.zh: 他的放縱最終毀了他的健康和事業。

senses.en: (logic) the set of qualities that define a word or concept
(old use) intensity; great mental effort

ex.en: In logic class, we learned that the intension of "triangle" is "a shape with three sides."
ex.zh: 在邏輯課上，我們學到「三角形」的內涵是「有三個邊的圖形」。

mn: 注意拼法：intension（內涵）≠ intention（意圖），發音相同。

senses.en: concentrated on one area in a short time; thorough
(farming) aiming to produce as much as possible from a small area

ex.en: She took an intensive Japanese course over the summer.
ex.zh: 她暑假上了一門日文密集課程。

mn: 常見片語 intensive care unit（ICU）：加護病房。

senses.en: something that you plan or mean to do

ex.en: I have no intention of quitting before the job is done.
ex.zh: 工作沒完成之前我沒打算放棄。

root.note: 把心思伸向某目標 → 意圖

senses.en: to communicate or work together
to have an effect on each other

ex.en: Children learn social skills when they interact with others.
ex.zh: 孩子在與他人互動時學會社交技巧。

root.note: 彼此之間互相作用 → 互動

senses.en: to speak or act on behalf of someone in trouble
to step in to help settle a dispute

ex.en: She asked the principal to intercede with the teacher on her behalf.
ex.zh: 她請校長幫她向老師說情。

root.note: 走到兩方之間 → 說情、調停

senses.en: to stop and catch someone or something before it reaches its destination

ex.en: The defender jumped to intercept the pass.
ex.zh: 防守球員跳起來攔截傳球。

senses.en: the act of speaking or acting on behalf of another

ex.en: Only the intercession of the embassy secured the prisoner's release.
ex.zh: 全靠大使館出面斡旋，那名囚犯才獲釋。

root.note: 走到兩方之間 → 調解

senses.en: a person who speaks or acts on behalf of another

ex.en: The village elder acted as an intercessor between the two families.
ex.zh: 村中長老擔任兩家之間的調解人。

root.note: 走到兩方之間的人 → 調解人

senses.en: to forbid something officially; to stop the movement of goods
[ˋɪntɚˏdɪkt] an official order forbidding something

ex.en: The navy tried to interdict shipments of illegal weapons.
ex.zh: 海軍試圖攔截非法武器的運送。

root.note: 在中間說話阻止 → 禁止

senses.en: temporary; serving until something permanent is arranged
the time between two events

ex.en: The board appointed an interim director while it searched for a new one.
ex.zh: 董事會在尋找新主任期間任命了一位代理主任。

root.note: 在兩者之間 → 過渡期

mn: 常見片語 in the interim：在此期間。

senses.en: a person who takes part in a conversation
a person who acts as a go-between in talks

ex.en: She was a thoughtful interlocutor who listened more than she spoke.
ex.zh: 她是個體貼的談話對象，聽得比說得多。

root.note: 在彼此之間說話的人 → 對話者

senses.en: a short period of time between two events
a short piece of music or performance between parts of a longer work

ex.en: The sunny afternoon was a brief interlude in a week of rain.
ex.zh: 那個晴朗的下午是一週陰雨中的短暫插曲。

root.note: 兩段之間的表演 → 插曲

senses.en: between two stages, levels, or points

ex.en: This class is for intermediate learners who already know basic grammar.
ex.zh: 這門課是給已經懂基礎文法的中級學習者上的。

senses.en: seeming to last forever, in a tiresome way

ex.en: We sat through an interminable meeting that lasted four hours.
ex.zh: 我們熬過一場長達四小時、沒完沒了的會議。

root.note: 沒有終點的 → 沒完沒了的

senses.en: a short break between parts of a play, concert, or film

ex.en: We bought snacks during the intermission.
ex.zh: 我們在中場休息時買了點心。

root.note: 在中間放開一段時間 → 中場休息

senses.en: to stop for a time; to suspend

ex.en: The fever seemed to intermit for a day before returning.
ex.zh: 燒似乎退了一天，後來又回來了。

senses.en: stopping and starting at irregular intervals

ex.en: The forecast calls for intermittent rain throughout the afternoon.
ex.zh: 天氣預報說整個下午會有間歇性降雨。

root.note: 中間有停頓的 → 斷斷續續的

senses.en: the insertion of words into a text or conversation
senses.zh: 插入的話語；（文本）竄改、增補

senses.en: (math) estimating a value between known values

ex.en: Scholars believe this line is a later interpolation, not part of the original poem.
ex.zh: 學者認為這一行是後人添加的，並非原詩的一部分。

root.note: 在中間加以修飾 → 插入、竄改

senses.en: to place something between two things
to interrupt a conversation with a remark

ex.en: The referee had to interpose himself between the two angry players.
ex.zh: 裁判只得站到兩名憤怒的球員中間。

senses.en: the act of placing something between others or of intervening

ex.en: The interposition of a mountain range protects the valley from cold winds.
ex.zh: 一道山脈橫亙其間，使山谷免受冷風吹襲。

senses.en: a person who translates speech from one language to another
a person who explains the meaning of something

ex.en: The president spoke through an interpreter at the summit.
ex.zh: 總統在高峰會上透過口譯員發言。

root.note: 在雙方之間協調的人 → 口譯員

senses.en: to question someone closely or aggressively

ex.en: Detectives will interrogate the suspect tomorrow morning.
ex.zh: 警探明天早上會審問嫌犯。

senses.en: having the form or function of a question
(grammar) a word used to ask a question

ex.en: For homework, turn each statement into an interrogative sentence.
ex.zh: 作業是把每個直述句改成疑問句。

senses.en: expressing a question
(law) a written question that must be answered under oath

ex.en: The lawyer sent a written interrogatory to the other side.
ex.zh: 律師向對方寄出一份書面質詢。

senses.en: to stop someone while they are speaking or doing something
to cause something to stop for a time

ex.en: Please don't interrupt me while I'm explaining the rules.
ex.zh: 我在解釋規則的時候請不要打斷我。

senses.en: to cross or divide each other

ex.en: The two highways intersect just north of the city.
ex.zh: 這兩條公路在城市北邊交會。

senses.en: (regional, New England) a low, flat area of land along a river
senses.zh: （美國新英格蘭方言）河谷低地

ex.en: The farmers grew corn in the rich soil of the intervale.
ex.zh: 農民們在河谷低地的沃土上種玉米。

senses.en: to become involved in a situation to change or improve it
to happen between two events

ex.en: The teacher had to intervene when the argument turned into a fight.
ex.zh: 爭吵演變成打架時，老師只好出面介入。

senses.en: the condition of dying without a valid will

ex.en: In cases of intestacy, the law decides who inherits the property.
ex.zh: 在無遺囑死亡的情況下，由法律決定財產由誰繼承。

senses.en: not having made a will before death

ex.en: Because he died intestate, his estate was divided according to state law.
ex.zh: 由於他死時沒有留下遺囑，他的遺產依州法分配。

senses.en: the long tube in the body that carries food from the stomach
(of conflict) within a country; internal

ex.en: Most nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine.
ex.zh: 大部分養分是在小腸被吸收的。

root.note: 身體內部的器官 → 腸

senses.en: a close, familiar, and affectionate relationship
a cozy, private atmosphere

ex.en: The small café has a warm intimacy that big chains lack.
ex.zh: 這家小咖啡館有種大型連鎖店沒有的溫馨私密感。

root.note: 最內心的關係 → 親密

senses.en: to frighten someone, especially to make them do what you want

ex.en: Don't let the size of the exam intimidate you.
ex.zh: 別被考試的份量嚇到。

senses.en: impossible to bear or endure

ex.en: The noise from the construction site was intolerable.
ex.zh: 工地的噪音讓人無法忍受。

senses.en: unwillingness to accept views or behavior different from one's own
(medicine) inability to eat or use a food or drug without bad effects

ex.en: The museum exhibit teaches visitors about the dangers of religious intolerance.
ex.zh: 這個博物館展覽教導參觀者宗教不寬容的危害。

senses.en: unwilling to accept views or behavior different from one's own
unable to eat or use something without bad effects

ex.en: He is intolerant of anyone who disagrees with him.
ex.zh: 他無法容忍任何和他意見不同的人。

senses.en: a substance such as alcohol that makes people drunk

ex.en: The law bans the sale of any intoxicant to minors.
ex.zh: 法律禁止販售任何致醉物給未成年人。

senses.en: to make someone drunk
to excite someone greatly

ex.en: Success can intoxicate a young star and make him arrogant.
ex.zh: 成功可能讓年輕明星沖昏頭而變得自大。

senses.en: located or occurring inside a cell

ex.en: Some viruses are intracellular parasites that can only live inside host cells.
ex.zh: 有些病毒是細胞內寄生物，只能在宿主細胞內生存。

senses.en: taking place within a single school or institution

ex.en: He plays on an intramural basketball team with his classmates.
ex.zh: 他和同學一起參加校內籃球隊。

senses.en: fearless and adventurous

ex.en: The intrepid explorers crossed the frozen sea on foot.
ex.zh: 這群無畏的探險家徒步穿越結冰的海洋。

root.note: 不驚慌發抖的 → 無畏的

senses.en: the quality of being complicated or detailed
(intricacies) the complicated details of something

ex.en: Visitors admired the intricacy of the carved wooden doors.
ex.zh: 遊客們讚嘆那扇木雕門的精緻繁複。

root.note: 纏進障礙中 → 錯綜複雜

senses.en: very complicated or detailed

ex.en: The rug has an intricate pattern of flowers and birds.
ex.zh: 這塊地毯有花鳥交織的精細圖案。

root.note: 纏進障礙中的 → 錯綜複雜的

senses.en: to arouse someone's curiosity or interest
secret planning of something harmful; a plot

ex.en: The strange title of the book will intrigue many readers.
ex.zh: 這本書古怪的書名會引起許多讀者的好奇。

parts.m: tricks, obstacles 詭計、糾纏（= tric）

root.note: 使纏進去 → 陰謀；吸引

senses.en: belonging naturally to something; essential

ex.en: The old letters have little money value but great intrinsic worth to the family.
ex.zh: 這些舊信件沒什麼金錢價值，但對這家人有很大的內在價值。

senses.en: serving to introduce a subject or begin something
(of an offer) available at a special price for a new product

ex.en: I signed up for an introductory course in psychology.
ex.zh: 我報名了一門心理學入門課。

root.note: 引領進入的 → 入門的

senses.en: (genetics) the movement of genes from one species into another through repeated interbreeding

ex.en: Scientists found evidence of introgression between wild and farmed salmon.
ex.zh: 科學家發現野生鮭魚與養殖鮭魚之間有基因滲入的證據。

senses.en: (formal) to put in, insert, or let in

ex.en: The valve is designed to intromit air but keep water out.
ex.zh: 這個閥門的設計是讓空氣進入，但把水擋在外面。

senses.en: to examine one's own thoughts and feelings

ex.en: After the loss, the coach asked each player to introspect and find ways to improve.
ex.zh: 輸球之後，教練要每位球員自我反省，找出改進的方法。

senses.en: the examination of one's own thoughts and feelings

ex.en: A long walk alone is a good time for introspection.
ex.zh: 獨自散步很久是自我反省的好時機。

senses.en: the tendency to focus on one's own thoughts and prefer quiet settings

ex.en: Introversion is not the same as shyness; many introverts are confident.
ex.zh: 內向和害羞並不相同，許多內向的人都很有自信。

senses.en: a quiet person who prefers to focus on their own thoughts

ex.en: As an introvert, she recharges by spending time alone.
ex.zh: 身為內向的人，她靠獨處來充電。

root.note: 心思向內轉的人 → 內向者

senses.en: to enter or interrupt where one is not welcome

ex.en: I'm sorry to intrude, but there is an urgent call for you.
ex.zh: 抱歉打擾了，有一通找你的緊急電話。

senses.en: the act of entering a place or situation where one is not welcome

ex.en: Many people see the new cameras as an intrusion on their privacy.
ex.zh: 許多人認為新裝的監視器侵犯了他們的隱私。
